newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia market watchdog to regulate unit trusts.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia market watchdog to regulate unit trusts.

text.p: Malaysia's Securities Commission said on Monday that it has been made the central regulatory authority for the unit trust industry as part of measures to promote the growth of investment vehicles.

In a statement, the market watchdog said: "To streamline the regulatory environment for unit trusts, the government has declared that a single regulatory authority would be responsible for the industry."

Other measures include enhanced disclosures in unit trust prospectuses, streamlining the regulation of advertisements and promotional materials, and the establishment of a regulatory framework to market and distribute unit trust products, it said.
The commission said it had consulted with the Federation of Malaysian Unit Trust Managers (FMUTM) and other authorities about regulating the marketing and distribution of unit trust products.

To encourage front-line regulation in the industry, the implementation and administration of the guidelines will be undertaken by the FMUTM, which has been given a grant of one million ringgit for initial assistance.

All persons wishing to market and distrubute unit trust products will have to register with FMUTM, the commission said. Full compliance with all the FMUTM guidelines will take effect from July 1, 1998.
"The above measures have been instituted to strengthen the framework for the regulation of unit trusts in the country, to ensure better protection for investors," the statement said.
Malaysia has more than 70 unit trusts with a total net asset value of 56.1 billion ringgit.
